newsitem.title: USA: PairGain jumps on talk of Lucent interest.
newsitem.headline: PairGain jumps on talk of Lucent interest.

text.p: PairGain Technologies Inc shares jumped five percent in active early trading Friday on market talk that Lucent Technologies Inc is preparing to buy the company, dealers said.
A spokesman for Lucent said the company would not comment on market rumors. PairGain executives were not available for comment on the speculation.

PairGain shares rose 1-3/16 to 22-1/16 and the stock was the most actively traded issue on the Nasdaq market with volume of 4.7 million. PairGain makes products which enable high-speed digital service over standard copper phone lines.
One trader in the options market said Friday speculation was that either Lucent or ECI Telecom Ltd, based in Petah Tikva, Israel, would buy PairGain.
No prices were being cited for the rumored deal.

However, the talk was enough to boost activity in PairGain call options, which investors often buy if they believe a share will rise, such as in an acquisition in which a bidder pays a premium over a stock's recent trading range.
Pairgain shares hit a 52-week high of 43-1/4 in the first quarter, but have since skidded as low as 14-5/8 as PairGain second quarter results fell short of analysts' estimates.

One source close to PairGain, which has been keeping a low profile in recent months, said the company has been in on-and-off talks with potential acquisitors over a long period, but he was not aware of any new developments.
"There have been some discussions. They usually don't amount to anything," the source said.

Some telecommunications investors and executives said recently they expect Lucent to become more acquisitive once it accounts for buyouts under the pooling of assets method, which occurs in October. This could set off bidding wars for some of the hottest technology firms.
Several analysts who cover telecommunications technology stocks discounted the acquisition rumors, with one attributing them to Wall Street bankers seeking to drum up business.

"I think there have been some underwriters out there who are spreading rumors," said Charles Pluckhahn, an analyst at brokers Dain Bosworth. "It's my strongly held belief that there's nothing to these rumors."

Pluckhahn, who has a "buy" recommendation on PairGain, said that, although the stock had also risen 2-3/4 on the initial rumors Thursday, it has been trailing recent gains elsewhere in the sector and was overdue to catch up.
Adtran, for example, has rebounded by more than 50 percent from its early June low of 21-3/4, while ADC Telecommunications has in recent sessions soared to double its late April level of $21-3/8.

UBS Securities analyst Nikos Theodosopoulos said the timing of the bid rumor -- after the stock recently slumped to one third of its 52-week high and while the company is in the process of launching a promising new copper-wire digital subscriber loop carrier system, known as PG-Flex -- argues against completing a deal.
"I don't see why the company would sell at this point," Theodosopoulos said of PairGain.

"I don't think that the company would sell itself with the stock so depressed, given that there's a possitive outlook with their new PG-Flex product," he said. "I would doubt that there's a major takeover pending, given that there's a very high confidence level with regard to that new product cycle."

PairGain said on Monday that the PG-Flex system had been approved for use at US West Communications Inc USW.O and he was aware of two other telecommunications companies who are preparing to use the product.
"If someone comes in and says here's $40 a share, obviously that's a different story," Theodosopoulos said.
(-sam.perry@reuters.com, in Palo Alto, +1 415 846 5400)
